clue.text: Fortunate to be up and about more?

definitions.meaning: lucky, favoured by fortune or heaven

definitions.text: to be up and about more?
definitions.meaning: someone up and about more spends less time in bed, read as the word bed with less placed inside it

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether being out of bed more often makes a person lucky.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: being up and about more means 'less' in 'bed', so LESS sits inside BED. There is no separate indicator word, so it works as a second, playful definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being blessed means enjoying good fortune, so the word is a synonym for lucky.

clue.text: There's nothing in a monkey pining

indicators.note: one piece goes in the other

parts.note: a langur is an Asian leaf monkey
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A captive monkey is wasting away from homesickness.
explanation.definitionFit: Languor is a listless weariness, the drooping state of someone pining.

clue.text: Top form

parts.note: the highest class in a British secondary school, taken by pupils of seventeen or eighteen

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top form' suggests peak condition, but it means the highest school class in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: In British schools the final years before university make up the senior class.

clue.text: Discourse on old sovereign

parts.note: ex means former, old
a sovereign is a British gold coin worth one pound

explanation.surface: A lecture about an antique gold coin.
explanation.walkthrough: A sovereign is an old British gold coin with a face value of one pound.
explanation.definitionFit: To expound is to explain at length, to discourse on a subject.

clue.text: One called to lay on fast food pudding?

parts.note: Mac or Mc is the prefix of a famous burger chain's products, standing for fast food
duff is a boiled pudding, as in plum duff

explanation.surface: Someone is asked to serve up a burger-chain dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lay on, Macduff' is Macbeth's famous challenge in Shakespeare's play, so Macduff is the one called to lay on. DUFF is a British word for a steamed pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's Macbeth the hero cries 'Lay on, Macduff', summoning the thane to fight.

clue.text: Rouse Scots cry to dismiss London leader?

parts.note: awa' is Scots for away, shouted to send someone off
Ken Livingstone was then the Mayor of London

explanation.surface: A Scotsman shouts to wake the capital's mayor and send him off.
explanation.walkthrough: Ken Livingstone was Mayor of London when this appeared, in 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: To awaken someone is to wake or rouse them from sleep.

clue.text: Yankee weapon or the European copy

parts.note: der is German for the, and German is a European language
a ringer, as in dead ringer, is a lookalike copy

explanation.surface: An American gun or a duplicate from the Continent.
explanation.definitionFit: A derringer is a small American pocket pistol named after its maker Henry Deringer.

clue.text: Former archbishop spoke of a split

indicators.note: the name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Geoffrey Fisher was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1945 to 1961

explanation.surface: An ex-archbishop talked about a schism in the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a split' looks like a church schism in the surface, but it is a crack.
explanation.definitionFit: A fissure is a long narrow crack, a split in rock or tissue.

clue.text: Failing at sport, nameless country gives rise to complaint among the older generation

definitions.text: gives rise to complaint among the older generation

indicators.note: a failing performance messes up the letters
'nameless' means without its name, and N is the standard abbreviation for name, so that letter is removed from the country

parts.note: England is a country

explanation.surface: A nation that keeps losing at games makes its older citizens grumble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Failing' rearranges AT SPORT into PROSTAT; ENGLAND without N, for name, gives EGLAND.
explanation.definitionFit: Enlargement of this male gland is a common ailment of older men.

clue.text: State accommodation in neat stone

indicators.note: one piece is accommodated, or housed, inside another

parts.note: neat is an old word for cattle, so an ox
NY is the abbreviation for New York State

explanation.surface: A government lodging is fitted out in tidy stonework.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neat' looks like an adjective meaning tidy, but it is the old noun for cattle, giving OX.
explanation.definitionFit: Onyx is a banded variety of chalcedony used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Everlasting cool celebrity on the box?

definitions.text: Everlasting cool celebrity on the box?

parts.words: Everlasting cool celebrity on the box?
parts.note: ground that stays frozen for good, playfully read as a permanent version of a famous television presenter whose surname means cold weather

explanation.surface: A television star is admired for never losing their composure.
explanation.walkthrough: David Frost was a famous British television interviewer, so a 'perma-Frost' is a celebrity on the box made permanent.
explanation.definitionFit: Permafrost is ground that stays frozen all year round, a lasting chill.

clue.text: "Shut up", as voiced in Afghanistan

indicators.note: read as 'in another form', the letters of the quoted phrase come out rearranged

explanation.surface: An order to be quiet is spoken in Afghanistan.
explanation.walkthrough: The weak anagram signal 'as' turns SHUTUP into PUSHTU; the quoted phrase looks like dialogue but is just the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Pushtu, also spelt Pashto, is a main language spoken in Afghanistan.

clue.text: Gambling debts can be plausibly deceptive

parts.note: spec, short for speculation, is a gamble
IOUs are written promises of money owed, so debts

explanation.surface: Betting debts can be a convincing kind of trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: Specious describes an argument that seems right but is actually false or misleading.

clue.text: A danger it constituted for one on stage

indicators.note: the letters are made up, or constituted, into a new form

explanation.surface: A risk faced by an actor performing in a play.
explanation.definitionFit: A tragedian is an actor who plays tragic roles, so a performer on stage.

clue.text: It warms one, getting extra lunch

definitions.meaning: an appliance that heats a room
gash is slang for spare or extra

explanation.surface: Someone stays warm by having a second helping at lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: GASH, meaning spare or extra, is mainly British and naval slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas heater is a domestic appliance that burns gas to warm a room.

clue.text: Contended outright with fever

indicators.note: read as 'out right', the letter R, short for right, is taken out

parts.note: to contend is to argue, so contended means argued

explanation.surface: Someone fought their case completely while running a temperature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outright' looks like an adverb meaning totally, but splits into 'out' and 'right': R leaves ARGUED.
explanation.definitionFit: Agued means afflicted with ague, a malarial fever with shivering fits.

clue.text: Doctor left in the middle of anxiety

indicators.note: the doctor has left, so those letters go out

parts.note: amongst means in the middle of
MO is a medical officer, a doctor

explanation.surface: A physician departs during a time of worry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the middle of' looks like it wants a central letter, but it is a synonym, AMONGST; removing MO leaves ANGST.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of deep dread or worry, a synonym for anxiety.

clue.text: Food for simpletons

definitions.meaning: noodle is slang for a fool

explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are pasta strips; noodle is also slang for a silly person.

clue.text: English road bending where all go for takeoff

indicators.note: the road bends, so its letters with E are twisted into a new order

parts.note: the proverb says all roads lead to Rome, so Rome is where all go

explanation.surface: A winding English road leads to an airfield.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bending' rearranges E and ROAD into AEROD; the proverb 'all roads lead to Rome' supplies ROME.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerodrome is a small airfield, the place aircraft use for takeoff.

clue.text: Shore up collapse underground — he was there

indicators.note: a collapse brings the letters down in a new order

explanation.surface: A tunnel needs propping up before it falls in on a man below.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapse' rearranges SHORE UP. Orpheus went down to the underworld to bring back Eurydice.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the musician Orpheus descended to Hades to rescue his wife.

clue.text: Master spy taken in battle

indicators.note: one piece is taken inside the other

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts
a spy is a secret agent

explanation.surface: A senior officer's spy is captured during the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: Magenta was an 1859 battle in northern Italy, which gave the dye its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The Battle of Magenta was fought in 1859 between France and Austria.

clue.text: Song and dance these days

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance
AD, anno domini, marks the present era

explanation.surface: Modern music and dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative poem or song, often sentimental.

clue.text: Joint assembly holds unexpected vote

indicators.note: the first piece holds the second inside it

parts.note: the Dail is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: an unexpected outcome jumbles the letters

explanation.surface: A parliament contains a surprise ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like an adjective meaning shared, but it is the woodworking noun. The Dail is Ireland's parliament, a convention worth knowing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dovetail is an interlocking carpentry joint with fan-shaped tenons.

clue.text: For local support many find wherewithal to cough up

parts.note: PH stands for public house, and a local is a pub
a leg supports a table or chair
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, so many

explanation.surface: A pub regular finds the money to pay up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cough up' looks like slang for paying, but here means literally coughing. A 'local' is British slang for one's regular pub; PH is a map abbreviation for public house.
explanation.definitionFit: Phlegm is the thick mucus brought up from the chest by coughing.

clue.text: Occupational disease caught from a metallurgist?

indicators.note: the letters are caught, picked up, from within the words

explanation.surface: A metal worker passes on an illness linked to the job.
explanation.walkthrough: The lurgi is a made-up infectious disease from The Goon Show, a 1950s British radio comedy.
explanation.definitionFit: The lurgy or lurgi is a jokey name for any unspecified illness.

clue.text: Build-up of gases — perhaps it's about time to clean flue?

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go about, around, the next piece
perhaps signals the letters might be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A chimney sweep decides soot has built up and the flue needs cleaning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges CLEAN FLUE into FLAULENCE, and 'about' puts it round T. The chimney picture hides the bodily sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Flatulence is an accumulation of gas in the stomach or intestines.

clue.text: What trains seldom do, victim of stunted development

definitions.meaning: trains rarely run to time, read as run plus T for time
the smallest, weakest animal of a litter

explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is cryptic: trains seldom 'run T', run on time.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt of a litter is the undersized animal whose growth lags behind its siblings.

clue.text: Rapid transit doesn't start on horseback

indicators.note: the word loses its starting letter

parts.note: rapid means fast
a ride is a journey, a transit

explanation.surface: A fast journey is delayed in setting off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doesn't start' drops F from FAST, leaving AST.
explanation.definitionFit: Sitting astride means with legs either side, as a rider sits on a horse.

clue.text: Christmas perhaps, not beginning of summer in the USA

indicators.note: the word is used without its beginning letter

parts.note: Christmas is an example of a festival

explanation.surface: Christmas falls in summer for some people, but not in America.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not beginning' removes F from FESTIVAL. Estival is the American spelling of British aestival.
explanation.definitionFit: Estival is an adjective meaning relating to summer, the US form of aestival.
